pace_grass.description: Paces back and forth to trigger encounters. Parametrized to handle any map and axis.

length.description: Number of steps in one direction before turning around.

iterations.description: Number of back-and-forth loops to execute.

pace_grass.python_script:
import json

axis = str(input_data.get('axis', 'horizontal'))
length = int(input_data.get('length', 2))
iterations = int(input_data.get('iterations', 5))

buttons = []
dir1 = 'Right' if axis == 'horizontal' else 'Down'
dir2 = 'Left' if axis == 'horizontal' else 'Up'

for _ in range(iterations):
    for _ in range(length):
        buttons.append(dir1)
    for _ in range(length):
        buttons.append(dir2)

print(json.dumps(buttons[:100]))

use_strength.description: Activates STRENGTH by backing out of any sub-menus with B, moving the cursor to Blastoise (Pokemon 2), selecting STRENGTH, and waiting. Includes conditional autopress logic.

autopress_buttons.description: If true, autopresses the resulting sequence.

use_strength.python_script:
import json

def run(input_data):
    # Safe sequence to back out of menus, open START, select POKEMON, select Blastoise (slot 2), select STRENGTH
    # This relies on the cursor returning to the START menu when we press B enough times
    buttons = []
    
    # 1. Spam B to get back to the overworld (3 times is usually safe from anywhere in the party menu)
    buttons.extend(["B", "B", "B"])
    
    # Wait for the overworld to load
    buttons.append("sleep 500")

    # 2. Open Start Menu
    buttons.append("Start")
    buttons.append("sleep 500")

    # 3. Select POKEMON (assuming cursor might be anywhere, but likely POKEDEX if just opened, or POKEMON if we just backed out)
    # The safest way is to go Up to Pokedex then Down to Pokemon.
    buttons.extend(["Up", "Up", "Up", "Up", "Up", "Up", "Up"]) # Guarantee Pokedex
    buttons.extend(["Down", "A"]) # Select Pokemon
    buttons.append("sleep 500")

    # 4. Select Blastoise (Slot 2)
    buttons.extend(["Down", "A"]) # Move to slot 2 and select
    buttons.append("sleep 500")

    # 5. Select STRENGTH (First option for a Pokemon with a field move)
    buttons.append("A")
    buttons.append("sleep 1000") # Wait for the text

    # 6. Clear text
    buttons.extend(["B", "B", "B"])
    
    print(json.dumps({"buttons": buttons}))

input_data = {} # Will be populated by the harness
run(input_data)
